remove_semantics.flow: Map delete first. If r>=D, T-- and move old last tracked slot to r unless equal. If r<D, inspect slot r entity bit0; if set P-- and move old prefix tail to r; then T--, D-- and move old dense tail to the resulting r. The -1 check is behind unsigned r<D and is unreachable for r=FFFFFFFF.

counterexamples.name: dense_delete_with_pending_tail
counterexamples.operation: Remove A_dense, valid map hit r=0, record bit0 clear. Original sets T=1,D=0 and skips final mover.
counterexamples.conclusion: B_pending is outside tracked [0,T), with stale map ordinal 1.

counterexamples.name: absent_key_aliases_ordinal_zero
counterexamples.operation: Remove absent X: delete helper returns 0 and changes no map bucket; caller treats 0 as A_dense ordinal.
counterexamples.conclusion: A_dense is dropped from tracked range though its map entry remains.

counterexamples.name: prefix_flag_mismatch_underflow
counterexamples.operation: Remove present ordinal 0; code tests record bit0 and decrements P before T/D.
counterexamples.conclusion: P wraps and first mover can use invalid source ordinal; partition/flag consistency is a necessary precondition.

finite_scope: Two complete remove bodies, one direct full map-delete helper, and prior pinned full mover ABI only.
limits: The static counterexamples do not prove runtime reachability.
Map presence, unique keys, valid ordinals, P/D/T ordering and record bit0 partition consistency are not established by these bodies.
Dense removal with D<T does not preserve every distinct tracked pending entity without another contract or repair.
No emitter, live hook, caller inventory expansion, or multiplayer verification.
